title: Pulitzer-recognized newsrooms use AI to sort evidence, not write the story
friendlyTitle: Top journalists use AI to find evidence, then check it themselves
summary: Nieman Lab reports that five 2026 Pulitzer winners and three finalists disclosed using AI, a record since disclosures began in 2024. Common uses included summarizing, translating, classifying, and searching large document collections, with reporters and specialists checking the relevant source material.
friendlySummary: Eight Pulitzer winners or finalists said they used AI. They mainly used it to search and organize many documents, not to write finished stories.
whyItMatters: This is a useful pattern for knowledge work: let AI sort a large pile and surface likely evidence, then have people verify the originals and own the final judgment. Disclosure and a clear boundary around AI-written output help preserve trust.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI is useful for finding the needle in a haystack. People should still read the source, check the facts, and make the final decision.
